predecessors.name: Kingdom of Ava
predecessors.text: Prome and the Irrawaddy country 'up to Tharrawaddy and Myede', seized from Ava by Thado Minsaw after Mingyi Swa's death in 1482

successors.name: Toungoo Empire
successors.text: Prome and its district, surrendered by Minkhaung on 19 May 1542

ledger.x: 1482: Thado Minsaw makes Prome a kingdom.
1532: the Confederation of Shan States comes down on its former ally.
1532: Prome becomes the Confederation's tributary and keeps its king.
19 May 1542: the siege ends in surrender.

wars.name: Confederation of Shan States attack on Prome
wars.outcome: Prome becomes a tributary of the Confederation (infobox: 'vassal of Shan states (1532-1542)') and keeps its own kings.

wars.name: Toungoo-Hanthawaddy War
wars.outcome: Toungoo conquers Hanthawaddy by 1541; Prome, which had sheltered Hanthawaddy troops in 1539, is besieged in late 1541 and surrenders on 19 May 1542.

wars.name: Toungoo siege of Prome
wars.outcome: Minkhaung of Prome surrenders on 19 May 1542; the kingdom ends.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes the Prome frontier: the page gives 'territories up to Tharrawaddy and Myede' and no boundary, and Cliopatria's three outlines differ by under 3 percent.
